description:
KCB §7 open question 3 (capability-bus.md ~line 256): subscription firehose backpressure / flow-control for high-volume-world subscriptions. Per-invoke cost is already handled by capability cost + grant spend ceilings (§2.1/§5); the spec currently parks firehose flow-control as 'an infra concern for the host's cost advisor.' This tasklist folds it into the contract ONLY on the next pressure break (ROADMAP.md Phase F6) — i.e. when a high-volume-world subscription scenario demonstrates that leaving flow-control purely to the host breaks a subscriber. PARKED: reactive by design; authored and held. KCB is candidate (0.3.0). Public-safe: bind roles.

**Unparked 2026-08-25 by operator decision.** The reactive-by-design discipline said to wait for a pressure test to force the question. US-1 IS that pressure test, and it is constructible today — so waiting was waiting for someone to do the work this tasklist describes. The trade is deliberate and worth stating: a manufactured pressure leg can force a question no real user has, so **US-2 folds a clause only if US-1 finds a CONCRETE break.** A leg that finds none closes the question as 'pressure applied, no break found', which is a real answer and a better one than an open note that never resolves.

userStories.title: A high-volume-subscription pressure leg forcing the backpressure question
userStories.description: Add the scenario leg where a high-volume-world subscription firehose breaks a subscriber, forcing the §7.3 flow-control question into the contract — KCB folds it only under pressure.
acceptanceCriteria: A scenarios/ leg drives a high-volume-world subscription (a firehose) and demonstrates the concrete break that leaving flow-control purely to the host's cost advisor causes a subscriber — the pressure that forces §7.3 into the contract.
The leg confirms per-invoke cost + grant spend ceilings (§2.1/§5) do NOT by themselves solve firehose backpressure, distinguishing this from the already-handled cost question.
It follows the scenarios/ convention and uses the KINP §3.4 placeholder namespaces; names no product.
userStories.notes: Wrote scenarios/kcb-subscription-firehose.md (focused pressure leg, 8 steps + findings). Verification observed green: node scripts/check-doc-integrity.mjs OK - 45 markdown files, 780 relative links checked, all 3 status tables match their headers; .chief/verify.sh --run selected guard-doc-integrity + guard-doc-links, both green (doc-links: 0 dead vs 0 on main), 'all selected gates green - allowing merge'; schemas parse ok. AC-1: 6 concrete deltas BP-1..BP-6, 2 blocking - BP-5 is the break AC-1 asks for (Step 6: SS8.1 parks flow control on the host's cost advisor, but SS3/ADR-0001 route-by-lookup-not-proxy keeps the host off the stream path, and under SS3.1 federation no single host has jurisdiction over both ends - the assignment is void, not deferred); BP-3 is the subscriber-side break (disconnect is the only lever, no resumption operand, a missed retraction leaves a claim asserted forever). AC-2: Step 2 shows cost+budget_units do NOT reach a stream - cost sits on params.capabilities[] and a subscription scopes to a world with no manifest object to price, and SS5 evaluates the ceiling 'at invoke' with no second invoke, so budget_units never decrements; and even extended it fails at the gate, i.e. a cliff not a brake. AC-3: KINP SS3.4 placeholders only (worldsim/analyzer/refkb/mediastore/orchestrator), no product named; scenarios/README.md table row + narrative added per convention.

userStories.title: Fold subscription backpressure into KCB §7.3
userStories.description: Reflect the pressure-forced flow-control decision into capability-bus.md's subscribe contract, bumping the version and staying candidate.
acceptanceCriteria: capability-bus.md's §7.3 / subscribe clause is edited to specify subscription flow-control / backpressure for high-volume-world subscriptions (e.g. subscriber-declared rate/window, provider signalling), consistent with the §2.1/§5 cost + grant model and the KCB §2 AgentCard-extension manifest.
The KCB version header is bumped and Status set to candidate with a changelog entry citing the scenario leg.
schemas/*.json still parse; if the subscribe manifest gains a flow-control field the schema twin is updated in lockstep, staying role-scoped with KINP §3.4 placeholder CURIEs.
userStories.notes: Folded BP-1..BP-6 into a new normative KCB §4.2 (a: optional port `volume` envelope, outside the schema_id digest as `cost` is; b: optional subscribe max_rate/max_in_flight/window/on_overflow under a normative lossless-vs-lossy rule, and a retraction is never shed; c: optional content-addressed `resume` operand a producer MUST answer resumed/gap-unavailable/resume-unsupported, never silently; d: ONE in-band control channel in both directions, which V-7's fold MUST ride rather than mint a second; e: metered subscription + brake-before-the-cliff; f: fetch fan-out composes onto delta L's pending-fetch tolerance; g: shape, not QoS). AC-1: §4.2 lands under §4 (the subscribe verb) rather than §7.3 — per iteration 1's finding the PRD's numbering is stale: §7.3 is Deprecation and backpressure was §8.1. §4.2 is consistent with the §2.1/§5 cost model (§4.2e gives the 'at invoke' ceiling its missing operand + evaluation point; a new §5 bullet carries it) and with the §2 AgentCard extension (`volume` is an optional port field in `params`; the extension URI does NOT move, per §2's added-optional-fields rule). AC-2: header bumped 0.4.6 -> 0.4.7 (patch: additive, 0.5.0 stays spoken for by §2.2's removal), Status Candidate, changelog entry cites scenarios/kcb-subscription-firehose.md by name and closes each delta; §8 resolved IN PLACE and now holds no open questions; the scenario's Resolution blockquote amended with a per-delta closure table. AC-3: schemas byte-unchanged and parse — koine ships no twin of the KCB card extension, and participant-self-description.schema.json is pointers-only with additionalProperties:false deliberately keeping the manifest payload out, so no `volume` field belongs there and no lockstep update fires. VERIFICATION OBSERVED GREEN: node scripts/check-doc-integrity.mjs -> OK, 45 markdown files, 790 relative links checked, all 3 status tables match their headers (capability-bus 0.4.7 candidate); `bash .chief/verify.sh --run` over the 6 changed files -> guard-doc-integrity + guard-doc-links both green, doc-links: 0 dead vs 0 on main, 'all selected gates green - allowing merge'; schemas ok (9 files parse). Fourth mirror (CLAUDE.md Current state prose, unchecked by CI) updated by hand and read back.
